Name: unit01:writing
JsonString: {"unit_id": "unit01", "prompt": "Write an essay of no less than 140 words on one of the following topics: Is smart technology making us dumb? / Will AI (artificial intelligence) cause mass unemployment? / Should parents monitor their children’s use of the Internet? The first topic has an outline that you can follow.", "outline": ["Introduction: present the controversial argument that smart technology is damaging our cognitive abilities, then state the thesis that it is actually making us smarter.", "Body: give three supporting points – smart technology helps us become more knowledgeable, helps us learn better, and helps us be more innovative.", "Refutation: address the worry that smart technology is making us dumb and explain why it is not supported by scientific evidence.", "Conclusion: restate the thesis that smart technology is changing our lives and benefiting us in positive ways."]}

Name: unit02:writing
JsonString: {"unit_id": "unit02", "prompt": "Write an essay of no less than 140 words on one of the following topics. One topic has an outline you can follow: an influential Chinese explorer. Develop your essay as a biographical narrative in chronological order, using time-order signals such as when, during, and later, and select only the details that best portray the person.", "outline": ["When and where the explorer was born", "How the explorer started his or her career", "What the explorer has achieved and what contribution he or she has made to China and the world", "Conclusion: the significance of the explorer to China and the world"]}

Name: unit03:writing
JsonString: {"unit_id": "unit03", "prompt": "Write a cause-and-effect essay of no less than 140 words on why reading books is important. Introduce the effect first, analyse the three causes in the body, and end with a short conclusion.", "outline": ["Introduction: state the thesis that reading books is important mainly for three reasons.", "Cause 1: Reading broadens our knowledge and provides experience that we can hardly have in our own life.", "Cause 2: Reading exercises our brains and improves our mental health.", "Cause 3: Reading increases empathy and makes communication more efficient, so reading is indispensable and we should all form the habit of reading."]}

Name: unit04:writing
JsonString: {"unit_id": "unit04", "prompt": "Write an essay of no less than 140 words on one of the following topics, using the point-by-point pattern of comparison and contrast developed in Text A. Topic: Continuing to study or going to work. One topic has an outline that you can follow.", "outline": ["Introduction: state the thesis that deciding whether to continue your studies or go to work will have different and profound impacts on your future life and career.", "Point 1: Your decision will influence the way you spend your time at college — continuing to study means more classes and campus life, while going to work replaces study time with office duties.", "Point 2: Your decision has financial implications — continuing to study involves tuition costs and delayed earnings, whereas going to work brings in a salary at once.", "Point 3: Your decision will have a great impact on your future job opportunities; conclude that you should be clear about these possible impacts before making the final decision."]}

Name: unit05:writing
JsonString: {"unit_id": "unit05", "prompt": "Write an essay of no less than 140 words on one of the following topics: “Curiosity and scientific breakthroughs” (an outline is given), “Procrastination is a bad habit”, or “Exploring the space for the benefit of all humankind”. Support your point with sufficient examples that are specific and typical, interesting and relevant, and arrange them in a clear order.", "outline": ["Introduction: State the thesis that curiosity is the secret to scientific breakthroughs.", "Body 1: Curiosity sparks questions that matter in scientific discovery - the example of Li Siguang and the Quaternary Glacial Theory of China.", "Body 2: Curiosity gives people the persistence to keep looking for discoveries - the examples of Michael Faraday and Tu Youyou.", "Conclusion: Curiosity plays a key role in important scientific breakthroughs."]}

Name: unit06:writing
JsonString: {"unit_id": "unit06", "prompt": "Write an essay of no less than 140 words on the negative effects of staying up late. Develop your essay as a cause-and-effect essay: state your thesis in the introduction, present the effects in the body from the least to the most important, and restate your position in the conclusion.", "outline": ["Introduction: Thesis statement – staying up late can do severe harm to us mainly in three aspects.", "Body: Effect 1 – negative impacts on our physical health; Effect 2 – lower work efficiency; Effect 3 – mental stress.", "Support each effect with details or examples from students’ daily life, and arrange them from the least to the most serious.", "Conclusion: Staying up late is by no means a good choice for us."]}
